identity.name: Lan Na Kingdom
native_names: เมืองล้านนา (Mueang Lanna)
alt_names: Kingdom of a Million Rice Fields

land.text: Mangrai's Ngoenyang around Chiang Rai (founded 1262 as his capital), which became Lan Na

predecessors.note: Ngoenyang has no Cliopatria row and no dossier; the Lan Na infobox lists it first among the predecessors. Mangrai reigned there 1261-1292 (Mangrai infobox).

land.text: the Mon kingdom of Hariphunchai (Lamphun), annexed in 1292 (Lan Na infobox)

predecessors.note: 162 of the 255 cells of Cliopatria's 1294 shape lie in Haripuñjaya's 1293 shape. The haripunjaya dossier ends in 1292 with the same event.

land.text: the same state and the same land (180 cells) after Mekuti's capture in November 1564: Lan Na under Burmese suzerainty, to the Siamese conquest of 15 January 1775 (Lan Na infobox)

successors.note: Not a new state: Cliopatria's 'Lan Na' row (1600-1761, shapes of 52,400-52,800 km2) shares Wikidata Q1059707 and the Lan Na article with this row. This dossier stops at 1564 because the 'lan-na' row belongs to another batch (se-01-h); the colour continues. Vassalage is not a handover: Lan Na 'became a vassal state of the Toungoo dynasty in 1558' (infobox 'Tributary of Burma (1st): 1558-1596'), which first-toungoo-empire draws as a tint over this land. See notes.

capitals.name: Wiang Kum Kam
capitals.note: Lan Na page: Mangrai stayed at Wiang Kum Kam 'until 1292 at which time he relocated to what would become Chiang Mai'; the Mangrai page has 'Wiang Kum Kam was founded' in 1294 and Chiang Mai's construction from 1296.

capitals.name: Chiang Mai
capitals.note: Infobox 'Capital: Chiang Mai (1296-1775)'. Mangrai 'founded Chiang Mai in 1296'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 1292-1293. The Lan Na infobox gives 'Acquisition of Haripunjaya: 1292' (the body 'in 1281', the Mangrai page 1291); Cliopatria starts in 1294. Its first shape is used since no page names a frontier.

Years only: 1294-1337. 73,682 km2 (255 cells): 162 cells from Haripuñjaya's 1293 shape plus Ngoenyang's Chiang Rai (39 cells) and Mae Hong Son (35), Lampang (18) and 93 cells in Laos. The Mangrai page's realm: 'Chiang Rai, Chiang Khong, Muang Lai, Chiang Kham, Thoeng (taken from Phayao), Haripunchai, Lampang (occupied by his troops), and Chiang Mai'; Phrae and Nan lay outside (Sukhothai's vassals). The Lan Na page also names Kengtung, Mong Nai and Chiang Hung as claimed. No infobox area to compare.

correction.text: shape without the eastern cities of Phayao that went to Nan; applies 1338-1352

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1338-1352. The 18 cells (5,287 km2) that the shape gains in 1344 are exactly Phayao's Cliopatria shape of 1332; the Phayao page dates the annexation to 1338 ('Khamfu then annexed Phayao into Lanna, while the eastern cities ... was annexed into Nan'). The Lan Na infobox also says 1338, its text says 1456 (Tilokaraj); 1338 stands. Review fix: the correction removes the 4 cells that went to Nan (the Phayao page); the ledger gain of 1338 takes the other 14 of Phayao's 18 cells.

correction.text: shape without the eastern cities of Phayao that went to Nan; applies 1353-1452

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1353-1452. The 94 cells (26,420 km2) lost in 1363 all lie in Cliopatria's Lan Xang of 1363 (93 of them in Laos). Lan Xang page: 'King Phayu of Lanna raised an army which Fa Ngum overwhelmed at Chiang Saen, forcing Lanna to cede some its territory' in 1353. Fa Ngum 'was crowned' in 1353. Cliopatria's date is 1363. Review fix: the correction removes the 4 cells that went to Nan in 1338 (see the 1344 keyframe).

52,577 km2: the same 180 cells as 1363 (only the outline vertices change, 30 to 36). The Ayutthaya-Lan Na War (1441-1474) was a see-saw over the northern cities ('Lan Na achieved limited territorial gains') that the shape does not draw; the ledger carries it as a contest. Includes the 4 cells that went to Nan in 1338 (see the 1344 keyframe); not corrected here.
52,549 km2: the 1363 outline again, 180 cells. No change in the cells. Includes the 4 cells that went to Nan in 1338 (see the 1344 keyframe); not corrected here.

52,577 km2: the same 180 cells, a different outline. Page: 'In 1507, Kaew invaded Ayutthaya but was repelled'; Ramathibodi II invaded in 1513 and sacked Lampang; no border change. Includes the 4 cells that went to Nan in 1338 (see the 1344 keyframe); not corrected here.
52,549 km2: the same 180 cells; Lampang was sacked in 1513 and 1546 (Lan Na page), not lost. Includes the 4 cells that went to Nan in 1338 (see the 1344 keyframe); not corrected here.

correction.text: shape without the eastern cities of Phayao that went to Nan; applies 1556-1563, to the end of Cliopatria's row

keyframe_review.note: Years only: 1556-1563 (Cliopatria's row ends in 1563). Mekuti 'surrendered on 2 April 1558' and the kingdom 'became a vassal state of the Toungoo dynasty in 1558'; he stayed king until 'captured by Burmese forces in November 1564'. The land stays the same 180 cells under Burmese suzerainty (infobox 'Tributary of Burma (1st): 1558-1596'), which the suzerain's ledger draws as a tint. Review fix: this keyframe was 'applies 1556-1558' with a loss of all the land to first-toungoo-empire and a dissolve in 1558; vassalage is the suzerain's vassal_start, not a loss. The four cells of the Yom headwaters (Pong, Chiang Muan) that the Phayao page gives to Nan in 1338 ('the eastern cities of Phayao along the upper Yom basin was annexed into Nan') are inside this shape; the correction removes them.

correction.text: shape unchanged; applies 1564, the year of Mekuti's capture, one year past the end of Cliopatria's row

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'The king was captured by Burmese forces in November 1564' and sent to Pegu; Bayinnaung made Wisutthithewi 'the queen regnant of Lan Na' (no year on the page). The state goes on; this dossier ends here and the 'lan-na' dossier continues the same land (see notes).

region.text: Ngoenyang (Chiang Rai) with Lamphun and the Ping valley

ledger.note: 1292: Mangrai's Ngoenyang becomes the kingdom of Lan Na with the annexation of Haripunjaya. The Lan Na infobox gives 'Acquisition of Haripunjaya: 1292'; 'He founded Chiang Mai in 1296, expanding it to become the capital of Lan Na'. The Mangrai page: Ngoenyang reign 1261-1292, Lan Na 1292-1311/1317. The page names cities, not a frontier.

1292: Mangrai takes Haripunjaya. 'subjugated the Mon kingdom of Hariphunchai' (body 'in 1281'), infobox 'Acquisition of Haripunjaya: 1292'; the Mangrai page: 'Mangrai defeated the Mon kingdom and annexed Haripunchai to his kingdom' in 1291, and the last king Yi Ba fled south to Lampang. The haripunjaya dossier records the same event in 1292.

1296: Mangrai founds Chiang Mai. 'Construction of Chiang Mai (lit. "New City") began in 1296'; the Lan Na infobox gives 'Founding of Chiang Mai: 1296'. The kings of Phayao and Sukhothai attended the founding ceremony (Phayao page).

region.text: the Phayao kingdom (Wiang Phayao and Wiang Namtao), minus its eastern cities that went to Nan ('the eastern cities of Phayao along the upper Yom basin'; read as the Pong and Chiang Muan area, 4 of Phayao's 18 cells)

ledger.note: 1338: Khamfu of Chiang Saen annexes Phayao. 'In 1338, Khamfu, the son of Saenphu ... invited Phaya Phanong of Nan Kingdom to attack Phayao. Khamfu then annexed Phayao into Lanna, while the eastern cities ... was annexed into Nan.' Cliopatria's 1344 shape gains exactly Phayao's 18 cells. Review fix: the region took the whole Phayao shape; it now subtracts the eastern cities, as the phayao-kingdom dossier does (its separate loss to nan-kingdom).

region.text: the part of Lan Na's 1362 shape that lies inside Cliopatria's Lan Xang of 1363 ('some of its territory', the Chiang Saen and Mekong lands)

ledger.note: 1353: Fa Ngum beats Lan Na at Chiang Saen. 'King Phayu of Lanna raised an army which Fa Ngum overwhelmed at Chiang Saen, forcing Lanna to cede some its territory.' The page names no land; the region is the 94 cells that Cliopatria's shape loses in 1363, all inside its Lan Xang.

region.text: Sawankhalok and Chaliang (Si Satchanalai), the northern cities fought over

ledger.note: 1451: Sawankhalok breaks away from Ayutthaya and joins Lan Na; Lan Na besieges Chaliang. The war's infobox runs 1441-1474; 1451 is the first dated ground ('Sawankhalok broke away from Ayutthaya and joined Lan Na. Lan Na besieged Chaliang (Si Satchanalai), but defenders repelled the attack'). The zone is the northern cities; the see-saw of 1459 (Lan Na takes Sawankhalok again) and 1460 (Ayutthaya reconquers Phrae) is not drawn.
1452: Ayutthaya captures Chiang Mai. 'Ayutthaya captured Chiang Mai, but was compelled to withdraw after Lan Na received help from Lan Xang.' The occupation lasted part of the year.
1452: Ayutthaya withdraws from Chiang Mai after Lan Xang helps Lan Na.

region.text: Sawankhalok and Chaliang (Si Satchanalai), the northern cities fought over

ledger.note: 1474: Lan Na retakes Chienjuen, 'putting an end to the conflict'. Result: stalemate with 'limited territorial gains' for Lan Na; the Lan Na page has 'Tilokaraj eventually sued for peace in 1475' and the infobox 'War with Ayutthaya: 1441-1474'.

1546: a prince of Lan Xang takes the throne of Lan Na. Rulers: 'Queen regnant Chiraprapha succeeded her husband around 1545'; 'Prince Xaysettha of Lan Xang reigned from 1546'; the Lan Xang page: 'Setthathirath, who in 1547 was crowned King in Chiang Mai'. The Mangrai line ends; the state stays Lan Na.
1551: Mekuti becomes king of Lan Na. Infobox 'Mekuti 1551-1564'; the page's text suggests he was installed after 1547.

region.text: Lan Na, the same 180 cells, which go on under the 'lan-na' dossier

ledger.note: November 1564: Mekuti is captured; the dossier stops (a boundary of the data, not the end of the state). 'The king was captured by Burmese forces in November 1564' (sent to Pegu); Bayinnaung made Wisutthithewi 'the queen regnant of Lan Na' (no year) and appointed Nawrahta Minsaw viceroy in January 1579 (infobox 1579-1607/08). The page runs Lan Na to the Siamese conquest of 15 January 1775 (tributary of Burma 1558-1596, of Ayutthaya 1596-1615, of Burma 1615-1628, independent 1628-1631, tributary of Burma 1631-1727, independent city-states 1727-1763, tributary of Burma 1763-1774) and the same Wikidata item as Cliopatria's 'Lan Na' (1600-1761). Review fix: the 2 April 1558 surrender is no longer a loss and a dissolve; it is a vassalage (first-toungoo-empire's vassal_start over lan-na-kingdom, 'Tributary of Burma (1st): 1558-1596'). If the orchestrator merges 'lan-na' into this dossier, drop this event and run to 1775.

wars.name: Mangrai's conquest of Haripunjaya
wars.outcome: Haripunjaya annexed to Lan Na; Yi Ba, the last king, fled south to Lampang.
wars.note: Dated 1281 (Lan Na body), 1291 (Mangrai page) and 1292 (Lan Na infobox); the ledger uses 1292. Mangrai used a merchant, Ai Fa, as a mole.

wars.name: Khamfu's annexation of Phayao
wars.outcome: Phayao annexed into Lan Na, its eastern cities into Nan.
wars.note: The Lan Na text's 1456 (Tilokaraj) disagrees with its own infobox and the Phayao page.

wars.name: Fa Ngum's war against Lan Na

zones.text: the part of Lan Na's 1362 shape that lies inside Cliopatria's Lan Xang of 1363 ('some of its territory', the Chiang Saen and Mekong lands)

wars.outcome: Fa Ngum overwhelmed Phayu's army at Chiang Saen and Lan Na ceded some territory.
wars.note: The Lan Na page does not mention the cession.

wars.name: Ayutthaya-Lan Na War (1441-1474)

zones.text: Sawankhalok and Chaliang (Si Satchanalai), the northern cities fought over

wars.outcome: Stalemate with limited territorial gains for Lan Na; Ayutthaya captured Chiang Mai in 1452 and withdrew; Lan Na took Sawankhalok in 1459; Ayutthaya reconquered Phrae in 1460; Lan Na retook Chienjuen in 1474.
wars.note: Intharacha died after Doi Ba (1460). The Lan Na page gives peace in 1475 and a surrender of Chaliang's governor to Tilokaraj in 1460.

wars.name: Ayutthayan invasions of Lan Na (1507, 1513)
wars.outcome: Kaew's invasion of Ayutthaya (1507) was repelled; Ramathibodi II invaded Lan Na in 1513 and sacked Lampang; no border change.
wars.note: Lampang was sacked again with Lamphun in 1546.

wars.name: Toungoo subjugation of Lan Na
wars.outcome: Mekuti surrendered on 2 April 1558 and Lan Na 'became a vassal state of the Toungoo dynasty in 1558'; he stayed king until 'captured by Burmese forces in November 1564'. No land changes hands.
wars.note: The page gives only the surrender date; the campaign's start is not on it. Review fix: vassalage (a tint in the first-toungoo-empire ledger), not a loss or an annexation.

certainty.note: A mandala of mueang around the Ping and Kok valleys: no treaty or survey fixes the frontier. The Phayao boundary (1338) and the Lan Xang cession (1353) are dated but not drawn as lines.

notes:
Cliopatria's 'Lan Na Kingdom' (1294-1563) and 'Lan Na' (1600-1761) share Wikidata Q1059707 and the Lan Na article (infobox Chiang Mai 1296-1775, with Burmese, Ayutthayan and Siamese suzerainties in turn), so they are ONE state. The 'lan-na' dossier belongs to batch se-01-h and did not exist on 2026-10-19, so this dossier was NOT merged with it: it covers the kingdom to Mekuti's capture in November 1564 (page-dated) and hands the same 180 cells to 'lan-na' with the same colour. Recommendation to the orchestrator (section 6 of the brief: one dossier under the earlier slug, both Names in cliopatria_names): merge 'lan-na' here, drop the 1564 dissolve and run to the Siamese conquest of 15 January 1775 (new keyframes for 1564-1599, 1619-1733 and 1762-1775, where Cliopatria has no Lan Na shape; the 180 cells hold throughout: the 1600 and 1734 shapes are 179 of them).
Review fixes (se-01-d review): (1) the 2 April 1558 loss and dissolve were removed. Lan Na page: 'Mekuti surrendered on 2 April 1558' and 'became a vassal state of the Toungoo dynasty in 1558'; he stayed king until 'captured by Burmese forces in November 1564'; the infobox runs the kingdom to 1775 with 'Tributary of Burma (1st): 1558-1596'. Vassalage is the suzerain's vassal_start: first-toungoo-empire must carry 'vassal_start 1558-04 over lan-na-kingdom' (tint) with the end in 1596 (Ayutthaya's tributary 1596-1615 is the ayutthaya-kingdom ledger's). The keyframe 1556 now applies 1556-1563 and a new keyframe covers 1564. (2) The 1338 gain of Phayao now subtracts the eastern cities that went to Nan (Phayao page); the later Cliopatria shapes keep those 4 cells, removed in the corrections of the 1344, 1363, 1556 and 1564 keyframes and noted on the others. I do not disagree with either finding. On the merge I follow the reviewer's minimum, not the 'preferably', because 'lan-na' is another batch's slug and the reviewer says the orchestrator must confirm.
Page budget (5) is exceeded by one page opened in error (the 1547-1549 war page, silent on Lan Na) and the Ngoenyang page opened for the predecessor; the review pass re-read the Lan Na, Lan Xang and Phayao Kingdom pages and opened Tilokaraj (2026-10-19). Lan Xang's page is shared with the Sukhothai dossier. No page gives an area, so the area check could not be made.
Gazetteer cell checks (not pages): the 1344 gain is exactly Phayao's 18 cells, 4 of them in the Yom headwaters given to Nan; the 1363 loss is 94 cells, all inside Lan Xang's 1363 shape; every later shape change (1453, 1459, 1507, 1512, 1556) leaves the same 180 cells.
Page conflicts: Haripunjaya 1281 (body), 1291 (Mangrai page), 1292 (infobox); Phayao 1338 (infobox, Phayao page) against 1456 (Lan Na text, Tilokaraj); Ayutthaya war 1441-1474 (infobox) against peace 1475 (Lan Na text); who retook Chiang Chuen (Sawankhalok) in 1474: 'Lan Na then retook the city' (war page) against 'Ayutthaya took it back in 1474' (Tilokaraj page); Mangrai's reign 1259/1261-1292 and Lan Na 1292 or 1296; Chaliang's governor surrendering in 1460 (Lan Na page, Tilokaraj) against the war page's 1459-1460 events; Wiang Kum Kam 1286-1292 (Ngoenyang infobox), 1292 (Lan Na text) or founded 1294 (Mangrai page).
Not drawn (undated or unresolved on the pages): Tilokaraj's 'Later he conquered Nan and Phrae' (Tilokaraj page, no year; the war page has Ayutthaya reconquering Phrae in 1460) and his westward expansion to the Shan states of Laihka, Hsipaw, Mong Nai and Yawnghwe, which the Lan Na page says then 'broke themselves free'; the Tilokaraj page (re-read 2026-10-19) says only that 'He also attacked Chiang Hung and the Shan region several times but could not impose control', with no year: no event, a gap for the shan-states dossier. Ngoenyang (Mangrai's kingdom, 1259-1292) has no row or dossier and is the predecessor. The Kengtung, Mong Nai and Chiang Hung 'claims' of the Lan Na page are not drawn.
